title: Most people remember Jericho for the moment the walls collapsed.
paragraphs: Most people remember Jericho for the moment the walls collapsed.

The sound.
The dust.
The sudden victory.
But that is not where the story begins.
And it’s not where the deepest lesson is hidden.

Because before the walls fell…
God gave an instruction that didn’t look like victory at all.
Walk.

Not attack.
Not strategize.
Not innovate.
Just walk.

Around a fortified city.
Once a day.
In silence.
If you pause and really think about that, it almost feels unreasonable.
This was not just any city. Jericho was shut up tight (Joshua 6:1). Its walls were thick, its gates closed, its defenses strong. From a human perspective, Israel needed weapons, tactics, force.
But God gave them a pattern instead.
And that’s the detail many people miss.

The breakthrough did not begin with power.
It began with obedience that felt repetitive… and quiet.
For six days, they walked.

No shouting.
No fighting.
No visible progress.
Just footsteps.
Can you imagine what that must have felt like?

Day one… anticipation.
Day two… curiosity.
Day three… questions.
Day four… doubt.
Day five… frustration.
Day six… silence stretched thin.
And still, the walls stood.
This is where many people would have stopped.
Because we often measure God’s movement by what we can see changing.
But Jericho teaches something deeper:
God can be working intensely… even when nothing looks different.

Every silent lap was not empty.
It was loaded with trust.

Every step was a declaration:
“God, Your way is better than what makes sense to me.”
And here’s the truth that hits hard:
Delayed visible results are not the same as delayed divine activity.

God was not waiting.
God was preparing.

Preparing the moment.
Preparing the miracle.
Preparing the people.
Because sometimes the wall is not the only thing God wants to move.
Sometimes He is shaping your discipline, your patience, your surrender.
And that takes time.
Then came the seventh day.
Seven laps.
Now the pattern intensifies.

Not because God needed more effort…
But because He was bringing them to a moment of release.
And only then—after days of silence, obedience, and repetition—God gave the command:
“Shout!” (Joshua 6:16)
And the walls fell.
Notice this carefully:

The shout was not what created the miracle.
It revealed the faith that had already been built in silence.
Read that again.
The shout revealed what the silence had produced.
That changes everything.

Because many people are waiting for a moment to shout…
But they are resisting the season of walking.

We want instant breakthroughs.
God often builds enduring faith.

We want one powerful moment.
God often works through consistent obedience.
Jericho reminds us:
The greatest victories in your life may be tied to the simplest instructions you keep repeating.

Keep praying.
Keep showing up.
Keep obeying.
Keep trusting.
Even when it feels like nothing is changing.
Especially when it feels like nothing is changing.
Because here is the hidden danger:

You can quit on day six…
Standing right next to a wall that would have fallen on day seven.
And you would never know how close you were.
That’s why this story matters so much.

It confronts our impatience.
It challenges our need for control.
It exposes how quickly we abandon what God said when results are not immediate.
But it also gives hope.
Because if God could bring down Jericho’s walls without a single human weapon…
Then your situation is not limited by your resources either.
God does not need your strength to do what He has promised.
He is looking for your obedience.
And obedience is not always loud.

Sometimes it looks like quiet consistency.
Sometimes it looks like unseen faithfulness.
Sometimes it looks like doing the same thing again… trusting that God is still in it.
So if you feel like you’ve been walking in circles…
If you’ve been praying and nothing has shifted…
If you’ve been obeying and nothing has opened…
Do not mistake silence for absence.
Do not mistake repetition for stagnation.
And do not mistake delay for denial.
Because Jericho proves this:
God can collapse in one moment what stood firm for a long time.
And when He does, it won’t be because you forced it.
It will be because you trusted Him long enough to see Him do it.
So keep walking.
Your sixth lap is not your final outcome.
Your silence is not your defeat.
And your obedience is not wasted.

Some walls don’t fall because you fight harder.
Some walls fall because you trusted God longer.
What “wall” in your life has God been asking you to keep walking around in faith… even when nothing seems to be changing yet?
